subject: Orion Health — Bridge playbook and executive comms for degraded inference (SEV-2)

From: Orion Health SRE <sre@orionhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@orionhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:45:12 -0800
Subject: [ORION] Elevated 5xx/timeouts for inference requests — possible SEV-2

Hi Markus,

We observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses and request timeouts from our integration starting ~08:30 PST. Error rates on Llama-13B-gen endpoint are ~12% and latency p95 has jumped to 1.8s (baseline ~400ms). This started after a deploy to our traffic simulator but looks correlated to request patterns rather than model change on our side.

Our SRE team confirmed this is impacting a subset of production user flows; we currently consider this a SEV-2. Could you please advise on next steps and open a bridge? We can provide request traces and our sidecar logs.

Affected region: us-west-2
Typical traffic: ~120rps
Contact: Daniel Park (engineering lead) — daniel.park@orionhealth.com

Thanks,
Orion Health SRE

Attachments: request-trace-08_44.log (link to shared bucket)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionhealth.com>, Samantha Lee <sam.lee@orionhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:15:40 -0800
Subject: Orion Health — Executive update: mitigation actions in progress (SEV-2)

Hi Daniel and Samantha,

Quick executive update from the bridge — summary and current state:

Summary:
- Impact: Intermittent 5xx and elevated latency affecting ~12% of inference requests for your Llama-13B endpoint in us-west-2. No data loss reported; inference outputs are degraded for a portion of requests.
- Scope: ~10% of sessions; primarily high-concurrency jobs.
- Severity: SEV-2 (service degraded, customer impact).

What we have done so far:
- Opened a dedicated incident bridge and are actively diagnosing (SUP-3245).
- Triggered autoscaler to add additional workers to your dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Validated that model binary and kernel selection align with expected releases; suspect runtime batching behavior under spike patterns.
- Implemented a temporary routing rule to direct 20% of traffic to q-llama-13b-v2 as a lower-latency fallback for non-sensitive routes.

Current ETA: we expect measurable reduction in error rate within 20–40 minutes; full restoration (<=1% error rate and p95 <=600ms) targeted within 90 minutes from now. We will update you if ETA changes.

Decision items for you:
1) Shall we proceed with failover to your secondary region (us-east-1) for critical traffic? This would add network egress latency but provide capacity if autoscaling is insufficient.
2) Do you need us to freeze billing for affected minutes while we remediate? We can fast-track a credit pending postmortem.

What we need from you: any recent changes to request patterns or simulation jobs that started ~08:15 PST. Request traces you can share are helpful — thanks for the initial trace file.

We will circulate a detailed timeline and root-cause hypothesis in the postmortem. I will provide another exec update in 30 minutes or sooner if there are material changes.

Respectfully,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
